Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The umpires are back out in the middle and the players of Australia Women have taken their places on the field. It will be the pair of Qiana Joseph and Hayley Matthews to open the innings for West Indies Women. Megan Schutt has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... The Run Chase ...

Right then! As the West Indies Women prepare to embark on their run chase, the question lingers in the air - Can they successfully chase down the target, or will the Australia Women's bowling unit rise to the challenge? The stage is set for a riveting second innings. Stay tuned as the run chase is up next shortly.

West Indies Women's plan started to work since they won the toss and chose to bowl first. Hayley Matthews drew the first blood and after that event, they started hunting the batters with the spin attack straight away. The pitch did not offer much of a turn or swings, but the lines and lengths of the bowlers were replying positive results for the Windies. After the drinks break things got a bit out of their hands but they got back as soon as Afy Fletcher eliminated Annabel Sutherland and broke the long and strong partnership. At the end of the inning, Aaliyah Alleyne and Afy Fletcher picked up two wickets each. Shamilia Connell, Karishma Ramharack and Hayley Matthews chipped in for one as well.

What a rollercoaster of an inning this has been! Firstly, Australia Women lost their top order in a pretty cheap way. Aussie batters looked to go for big shots but were not able to execute their plan. Within the first half of the first inning, they lost half of their batters. But the game changed when Ash Gardner and Annabel Sutherland brought composure to the track. They anchored the inning outstandingly and pulled the game from 59 for 5 to 117 by the 17th over with all their experience. Their rugged partnership helped the side pull the strings and provide something to challenge in the later inning. After the partnership broke, the Aussies once again lost the tempo. However, The lower middle order did enough to end up scoring 144 runs on the board. The skipper, Alyssa Healy must be happy as things have turned from bad to better for the side.

Swing and a miss! Outside leg, full in length, King swings but doesn't connect and steams off to the other end and completes the run. The keeper collects the ball on a couple of bounce, runs forward for a run out but Tayla Vlaeminck is quick to reach home in the end. A good decent finish for Australia Women, given how they were struggling in the first half.

Looking ahead to the main tournament, Australia Women will compete in Group A alongside India, Sri Lanka, New Zealand, and Pakistan Women. Meanwhile, the West Indies Women have been placed in Group B, which includes South Africa, England, Scotland, and Bangladesh Women. This final warm-up match serves as a critical dress rehearsal for both teams. It's their last chance to fine-tune tactics, test different combinations, and lock in their optimal playing XI before the official competition gets underway. With all said, stay tuned for the toss and team updates.

The Australian Women team comes into this match with high spirits, fresh off a commanding victory against their longtime rivals, England Women. Their batting prowess was on full display, with Beth Mooney leading the charge and strong performances from Tahlia McGrath and Ashleigh Gardner. Australia's lineup is formidable, boasting versatile all-rounders such as Ellyse Perry and Annabel Sutherland, while their potent bowling attack adds to their overall strength, making them a tough team to beat in their title defence, and of course, one of the favorites in the title contention.

West Indies Women are coming off a defeat against India Women in their first warm-up clash and would want to make amends in the result this time around to enter the main competition with some positive momentum. The seasoned Hayley Mathews will lead the side as usual. She took 4 wickets and bowled impressively, but would want to make some mark with the bat as well. Chinelle Henry, the half-centurion from the previous game will be accompanied by a robust batting order including Shemaine Alteia Campbelle. Apart from Hayley, the other bowlers will aim to make some impact as well.

It is the final day of the warm-up games before we kickoff the real action in the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup, 2024 on the UAE soil. On that note, we welcome you all joining us in the coverage of the practice match that features West Indies Women taking on Australia Women at The Sevens Stadium, Dubai.
